claim: SEC FTD files are pipe-delimited half-month files (a: first half posted at month end; b: about the 15th of the next month) listing every security with a non-zero balance since 2008-09-16; the price field is the previous day close; the SEC says fails arise on long and short sales and are not evidence of naked shorting.
quote: fails-to-deliver can occur for a number of reasons on both long and short sales. Therefore, fails-to-deliver are not necessarily the result of short selling
limitations: Page extract via WebFetch summariser (raw curl was rate-limited with HTTP 403); the extract preserves the field list and the quoted caveat.
impact_on_spec: The sign (high FTD -> lower return) is preregistered from the literature; effect sizes were not read so no target is taken; shortability and the 15-day publication lag are the reasons a cheap IC gate precedes any book.

claim: Reg SHO threshold security: aggregate fail-to-deliver position at NSCC for five consecutive settlement days of 10,000 shares or more equal to at least 0.5% of shares outstanding; the FTDSH signal (fails / shares outstanding) is a continuous version of that ratio.
quote: an aggregate fail to deliver position at a registered clearing agency (i.e., National Securities Clearing Corporation) for five consecutive settlement days of 10,000 shares or more that is equal to at least .5% of the security
limitations: Definition page; says nothing about returns.
impact_on_spec: The sign (high FTD -> lower return) is preregistered from the literature; effect sizes were not read so no target is taken; shortability and the 15-day publication lag are the reasons a cheap IC gate precedes any book.

claim: Stratmann and Welborn (J. Empirical Finance 2016): stocks with fails-to-deliver experience negative abnormal returns proportional to their FTD levels (event study and Fama-French portfolio analysis); short sellers of low and high FTD stocks obtain positive estimated profits net of proprietary borrow costs; FTDs reflect nonbinding short sale constraints.
quote: stocks with fails-to-deliver (FTDs) experience negative abnormal returns that are proportional to their FTD levels
limitations: Abstract page only (full text paywalled); sample period, horizon and effect size not read; period of the study predates 2019 and uses proprietary borrow-cost data we do not have.
impact_on_spec: The sign (high FTD -> lower return) is preregistered from the literature; effect sizes were not read so no target is taken; shortability and the 15-day publication lag are the reasons a cheap IC gate precedes any book.

claim: Autore, Boulton and Braga-Alves (Financial Review 2015): stocks reaching threshold levels of failures become significantly overvalued, with reversals where short-sale constraints bind, but the mispricing is likely difficult to arbitrage because of extreme shorting costs.
quote: the mispricing is likely to be difficult to arbitrage because of extreme shorting costs
limitations: Abstract page only; threshold-list stocks (a tail of FTD), pre-2015 sample; effect size not read. Supports the sign (high FTD -> lower later return) and the shortability warning.
impact_on_spec: The sign (high FTD -> lower return) is preregistered from the literature; effect sizes were not read so no target is taken; shortability and the 15-day publication lag are the reasons a cheap IC gate precedes any book.
